title: Responder engagement lifecycle, rota rules, and communications handbook
author: Marcus Chen
content:
Summary:
This handbook documents the lifecycle for responder engagement at Redwood Inference: how on-call rotas are created and maintained, responder responsibilities during incidents, runbook fast-paths for common degradations, a practical postmortem timeline, game-day exercise design, and ready-to-send status page and customer communication templates. It is intended for SREs, owners of customer-facing services, incident commanders, and engineering managers.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all production-facing services in Redwood-hosted and Dedicated offerings.
- Covers incidents that meet our SLO alert thresholds (see Appendix).
- Provides concrete templates, checklists, and an exercise syllabus to keep responder muscle memory sharp.

Definitions and roles:
1. First Responder (FR): Primary on-call engineer who triages and performs initial containment.
2. Service Owner (SO): The team responsible for root cause analysis and long-term fixes.
3. Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates responders, customer comms, and major decisions. Picks a single restoration goal and a communications cadence.
4. Bridge Lead (BL): Manages the incident bridge/virtual room and logs decisions.
5. Communications Lead (CL): Drafts status page and customer updates; works with PR/CS for external messaging.

Incident lifecycle (high-level):
1) Detection and Triage (T+0): Alert fires. On-call FR acknowledges within target: 1 minute for Sev1, 5 minutes for Sev2.
2) Containment (T+<15m): FR executes containment runbook (see Fast-path runbooks). If containment successful, IC may declare a degraded but contained state.
3) Escalation (T+15–30m): If containment fails, FR escalates to SO and IC. IC sets Restore Objective and cadence (e.g., status every 30m).
4) Restore (T+30m–hours): Work to restore service to SLO. Use fallbacks where available: model-variant routing, capacity failover, or degraded feature toggles.
5) Post-incident (T+1–72h): Short stabilization check, assemble timeline, and draft postmortem.
6) Long-term fix (weeks): Schedule corrective tasks and track to completion.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Sev1: FR -> IC within 5m -> Pager to SO lead -> Eng Director notified at 60m if unresolved.
- Sev2: FR -> IC within 15m -> SO notified within 1h.
- Sev3: Email and ticket, SO triages normal hours.

Rota management rules (practical):
- Rotation length: 7 days for standard responders; 2-week shifts reserved for teams with low headcount and manager approval.
- Handoff window: 15 minutes before and after shift boundary for shadowing; outgoing FR posts Handoff Checklist to the bridge.
- Time off and swaps: Use the rota web UI to request swaps; swaps require both engineers' approval and a manager sign-off if swap reduces coverage below N-1.
- Escalation coverage: Each primary must nominate a secondary (buddy) with overlap on the calendar.

Handoff checklist (outgoing to incoming):
- Current incident list (IDs + short status) and active bridges.
- Outstanding alerts with mute/acknowledgement status.
- Known flaky signals (e.g., metric X with expected spikes after nightly jobs).
- Pager and Slack channel confirmations.
- Location of runbooks and active tickets (link + owner).
- Any customer escalations in progress.

Fast-path runbooks (examples):
- High request latency on text-generation endpoints:
  1. Check recent deploys: curl -s https://deployments.internal/api/latest | jq .
  2. Confirm model pool utilization: /ops/gpu-metrics dashboard -> look for >85% sustained.
  3. If model pool saturated: enable burst pool for 10m (CLI): redwoodctl capacity burst --pool inference-burst --duration 10m
  4. If KV cache fill causing eviction storms: toggle cache-metrics logging and roll back last quantization change.
  5. Restore target: P95 latency < 400ms for standard profiles.
- Error spike in embeddings pipeline:
  1. Check schema changes and recent client commits.
  2. Re-run a small batch in staging and compare logs.
  3. If schema mismatch: script to drop/transform bad records (examples at /services/embeddings/tools/transform.py).

Game-day exercises (quarterly cadence):
- Objective: Validate decision-making chain (FR -> IC -> CL) and verify status templates under pressure.
- Frequency: Quarterly full-simulations; monthly focused drills for high-risk services.
- Example scenario: Multi-region model-serving fallback fails; team must execute routing policy change and craft a 2-line customer notice within 20 minutes.
- Scoring rubric: Time to containment, clarity of IC decisions, quality/timeliness of customer comms.

Postmortem timeline and template:
- Within 24 hours: IC and BL produce 1-paragraph incident summary + timeline + known root cause ID (draft).
- Within 72 hours: Draft postmortem including RCA, contributing factors, corrective actions, and owner assignments.
- Within 2 weeks: Postmortem review meeting; publish final document and link it to the ticket/epic.

Postmortem template (copyable):
- Title: [SevX] Short description — YYYY-MM-DD
- Summary: 2–3 sentences describing customer/user impact and scope.
- Timeline: ordered events with timestamps (detection, key actions, restore).
- Root cause: succinct cause statement.
- Contributing factors: list (human, process, technical).
- Corrective actions: owner, target date, verification steps.
- Follow-ups: related tasks/epic links.
- Metrics: pre/post SLO metrics and signal charts.

Status page and customer communication templates (practical):
1) Initial acknowledgement (short, public):
- Title: Incident: [service-name] degraded — investigating
- Body: We are aware of increased errors/latency for [service-name]. Our team is investigating. We will update this page at least every 30 minutes. Impact: Some API requests may fail or be slower than normal.

2) Customer-facing update (20–40 minutes after detection):
- Subject: Update: [service-name] degraded — mitigation in progress
- Body: Our engineers have identified a likely cause (e.g., regional capacity pressure). Steps taken: enabled burst capacity, routed traffic to healthy pools, and are monitoring for stabilization. Expected next update: in 30 minutes.

3) Resolution notice (public):
- Title: Resolved: [service-name] — incident closed
- Body: The root cause was [short cause]. Service has been restored to normal levels as of [timestamp]. Impact: [brief note about customer ops]. Follow-up: A postmortem will be published within 72 hours.

Internal CL -> CS quick template when customers are escalated:
Subject: Action required: Customer [customer-name] affected by [incident-id]
Body: Short summary, customer scope, any mitigation provided, RCA ETA, next internal contact.

Quality expectations for comms:
- All public updates must be factual and avoid technical jargon. Avoid promising timelines for full RCA.
- Customer-specific replies should be coordinated with CS/PR for enterprise accounts.

Appendix: SLO thresholds and alerting guidance:
- Availability SLO (example): 99.95% per calendar month for hosted API core endpoints.
- Severity mapping:
  - Sev1: Any event that causes >5% of customer-facing requests to fail or total outage for >5 minutes. Pager triggers: error-rate >5% sustained for 2m or p95 latency >1s for 5m.
  - Sev2: Degraded experience affecting <5% or intermittent errors. Alert trigger: error-rate >1% for 5m.

Operational tooling links and commands (examples):
- Open incident bridge: https://bridge.internal/new?incident=true
- Search recent deploys: redwoodctl deploy list --service [service-name] --since 24h
- Mute noisy alerts: alertsctl mute --alert [ALERT_ID] --duration 30m  (only IC or manager may mute a service-wide alert)

Governance and measurement:
- Monthly oncall health review: teams publish metrics (avg response time, handoff compliance, number of swaps) to the SRE dashboard.
- Postmortem quality score: each postmortem is reviewed by SRE leads and given a score (0–5) on signal completeness and actionability. Score <3 requires follow-up remediation.

Appendix B: Example customer status update (text block ready to paste):
- "We are investigating an increase in error rates for Redwood API text-generation endpoints impacting a subset of requests. Engineers have implemented temporary routing changes and are monitoring. We expect reduced errors within the next 30–60 minutes. If you are seeing critical failures, please contact support@redwood.ai with incident ID RED-20250302-47."

Related resources and links:
- Runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index
- Incident tickets and postmortem archive: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-archive
- Rota management UI: https://rota.internal/

Ownership and review cadence:
- Document owner: Engineering SRE guild (oncall working group).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review or after any Sev1 incident.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-12: Created by Marcus Chen (initial draft).
- 2025-02-20: Added postmortem timeline and updated severity thresholds (reviewers: Priya Raman, Lena Ortiz).
- 2025-03-02: Finalized customer comms templates and published.

Notes for teams implementing runbooks:
- Keep runbook steps concrete and auditable (commands, dashboard links, expected metric deltas).
- Avoid single-person dependent steps; every critical step must have an alternative approver.
- Label runbooks with "last_validated: YYYY-MM-DD" so teams know when to refresh them.

End of document.
